plain.li: {ENVIED_nameDef} has one now, and I've been looking at it every day since.
If {ENVIED_nameDef} could ask and get one, I thought I'd try my luck as well.
I'm not jealous of {ENVIED_nameDef}, I'd just like the same, that's all.
[trait:Jealous] Everyone keeps telling me how nice {ENVIED_nameDef}'s is, as if I hadn't noticed.
[newcomer] I'm new here, but I've seen what {ENVIED_nameDef} was given, and I'd like my turn.

warm.li: I asked {ENVIED_nameDef} how it felt to get one, and the answer made me want to ask too.

blunt.li: {ENVIED_nameDef} has one, so put my name down next.

cheerful.li: {ENVIED_nameDef} showed me {ENVIED_possessive}, and I've been thinking about it ever since.

gloomy.li: I watched {ENVIED_nameDef} get one and told myself I didn't mind, which wasn't true.

cold.li: {ENVIED_nameDef}'s request was granted, so mine should be judged by the same standard.

plain.li: You promised me "{WISH}", and I told people it was coming.
I waited because you promised, and now I've nothing to show for the waiting.
I'll remember this promise longer than you did.
I trusted the council more than most, and this is what it gets me.
A promise from the council turns out to be worth about as much as a no.

warm.li: I'd have understood a no, but I can't understand a promise that just went away.

blunt.li: You broke your word, and I'll not forget it.

cheerful.li: So much for counting the days, then.

gloomy.li: I should have known better than to hope, after all this time here.

cold.li: The promise lapsed, and I'll weigh the council's next one accordingly.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} has "{WISH}" already, and I'm still waiting on "{MINE}".
I asked first, but I suppose {OTHER_nameDef} asked louder.
Funny how {OTHER_nameDef}'s request went straight to the top of the pile.
[trait:Jealous] I saw {OTHER_nameDef} get it, and I'll be thinking about that for a while.
There must be a list somewhere, and I'd like to know who wrote my name so far down it.

warm.li: I'm glad for {OTHER_nameDef}, truly, but I was hoping it would be my turn first.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} jumped the queue, and everybody saw it.

cheerful.li: Good news for {OTHER_nameDef}, and I'll take it as a sign mine is coming soon.

gloomy.li: Of course {OTHER_nameDef}'s came first, mine never does.

cold.li: I asked earlier, so I'd like to know what {OTHER_nameDef} had that I didn't.

plain.li: Good, I'll stop bringing up "{WISH}" at every meal.
Then I'll take you at your word and wait a little longer.
[repeat] At last, after all the times I've asked.
[petition] I'll tell the others who put their names to it, they'll be glad to hear.
I'll tell the others it's coming, so don't make a liar of me.

warm.li: Thank you for listening, it means a lot that someone did.

blunt.li: Good, now see that it happens.

cheerful.li: I knew if I asked nicely enough it would come round.

gloomy.li: [bitter] Another promise, and I'll believe this one when it's in front of me.

cold.li: Then I'll expect it, and I'll ask again if it doesn't come.

plain.li: I stopped waiting for "{WISH}" and got on with it myself.
It took me a while, but I've seen to it with my own hands.
Nobody else had the time, so I made the time myself.
I'd rather have had help, but it's done now and that's what matters.
[trait:Lazy|trait:Slothful] I've done it myself, and you've no idea how much that cost me.

warm.li: I knew everyone was busy, so I sorted it out and didn't want to make a fuss.

blunt.li: Waited, got nothing, did it myself.

cheerful.li: It turns out I'm quite handy when nobody else is available.

gloomy.li: I did it myself, and nobody even noticed I'd been waiting.

cold.li: I've dealt with it myself and saved the council the trouble of deciding.

plain.li: I've asked the council for things before, and I've stopped keeping count of the answers.
They say the council is there for everyone, but it's never been there for me.
[lowmood] I'm tired, I'm fed up, and the council is the last place I'd go for help.
I put my name to things, and the council puts them at the bottom of the pile.
The council has its favourites, and I'm not one of them.

warm.li: I want to trust the council again, I just don't know how any more.

blunt.li: The council can sort out its own problems, since it won't sort out mine.

cheerful.li: Ask the council for something, I dare you, and see how long you wait.

gloomy.li: Nothing I say to the council ever changes anything.

cold.li: I've stopped counting on the council, and I've arranged things accordingly.
